title: Injury Prevention, Safe Training Techniques, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport in Trail Runners
claims: Most acute and chronic trail running musculoskeletal injuries occur in the lower leg, primarily the knee and ankle; more than 70% are overuse injuries, and ankle sprains are the most common acute injury.
Key mechanisms underlying injury and progression include inadequate neuromotor control, balance and coordination, running through fatigue, and abnormal kinematics on variable terrain.
Real-time adjustments to cadence, step length and knee flexion on the trail may mitigate impact-related injury risk.
Multicomponent prehabilitation combining dynamic flexibility, neuromotor strength and balance, and plyometrics fosters stable, controlled movement on trails.
